record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.context_brief: Jones polynomial detection of the unknot
record.original_question: Does there exist a knot in the 3-sphere S^3, distinct from the unknot, whose Jones polynomial is equal to the Jones polynomial of the unknot?

evidence.quote: Does there exist another knot in the 3-sphere with the same Jones polynomial as the unknot?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^3$ denote the 3-sphere, and let $K \subset S^3$ be a tame knot. Recall that the Jones polynomial $V_K(t) \in \mathbb{Z}[t^{1/2}, t^{-1/2}]$ is the Laurent polynomial invariant defined on oriented knots by the skein relation
$$t^{-1} V_{L_+}(t) - t\, V_{L_-}(t) = (t^{1/2} - t^{-1/2}) V_{L_0}(t),$$
together with the normalization $V_{\mathrm{unknot}}(t) = 1$. 

Question: Does there exist a knot $K \subset S^3$ that is not isotopic to the unknot but satisfies $V_K(t) = 1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem—commonly called the Jones unknot problem—remains open. It has been verified that every prime knot with up to 24 crossings has non-trivial Jones polynomial, and Khovanov homology is known to detect the unknot (Kronheimer–Mrowka), but whether the Jones polynomial itself detects the unknot is still unresolved as of 2025; even the 4-strand braid case is open.

status_evidence.snippet: Every prime knot with up to 24 crossings... is known to have a non-trivial Jones polynomial... It is not known whether the Jones polynomial detects the unknot.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether the Jones polynomial detects the unknot remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: In braid presentation, the case of 4-strand braids is already open.
status_evidence.claim: The 4-braid case of the Jones unknot conjecture remains open as of 2025.
